Henrik Ibsen, Hedda Gabler, translated by Edmund Gosse and William Archer.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/henrik-ibsen/hedda-gabler/edmund-gosse_william-archer

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Henrik Ibsen, an author, died 1906.
- Edmund Gosse, an annotator and translator, died 1928.
- William Archer, an annotator, translator and writer of the introduction, died 1924.

First publication of the text used: 1891 (SE colophon: 'Hedda Gabler was published in 1890 by Henrik Ibsen. It was translated from Danish in 1891 by Edmund Gosse and William Archer.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1891. The edition's own statement of rights (quoted below) says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name the country of first publication. The possible countries are Norway and Denmark, the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each has a term of life + 70 years or less. The last person to die did so in 1928, so the text is public domain in each of them.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon (quoted above): publication year 1891.
